title: 3  Existing Fish Observations within the Kenai Borough
text:
3.1 ADFG AFFI Data
This script explores data sources for existing freshwater fish presence/absence data on the Kenai Peninsula, including from the following sources:
We are interested to see which, if any, of these datasets are applicable to End of Anadromy and/or end of Fish modeling.
The following sections perform data intake for each data source seperately, and harmonize it into a single dataframe.
Alaska Department of Fish and Game’s Alaska Freshwater Fish Inventory: https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/index.cfm?adfg=ffinventory.main
Show code
# Reads pre-processed GeoPackages derived from AFFI_DataExport_8Aug2024.xlsx
# and kpb_boundary shapefile. If source data changes, re-run the affi-parse-raw
# chunk below to regenerate affi_clipped.gpkg, then re-render this document.
affi_harmonized <- st_read("data/input/fish_obs/affi/affi_clipped.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)

kpb_boundary <- st_read("data/input/kpb_boundary/kpb_boundary.gpkg", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(4326)
Show code
# Re-run this chunk only if AFFI_DataExport_8Aug2024.xlsx is updated.
# Parses the raw AFFI relational database, harmonizes species names,
# clips to KPB, and writes affi_clipped.gpkg.
# Note: this code was originally generated with AI assistance (ChatGPT, 3/4/2026)
# due to the complex multi-tab relational structure of the AFFI export.
dat <- "data/input/fish_obs/affi/AFFI_DataExport_8Aug2024.xlsx"

site      <- read_excel(dat, sheet = "Site")
survey    <- read_excel(dat, sheet = "Survey")
fish_obs  <- read_excel(dat, sheet = "Fish Observation")
fish_ind  <- read_excel(dat, sheet = "Fish Indivual")
fish_add  <- read_excel(dat, sheet = "Fish AddCount")
samp_evt  <- read_excel(dat, sheet = "Sample Event")
observer  <- read_excel(dat, sheet = "Observer")

normalize_person_name <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  x[x == ""] <- NA_character_
  out <- vapply(x, function(s) {
    if (is.na(s)) return(NA_character_)
    s <- str_squish(s)
    parts <- unlist(str_split(s, "\\s+"))
    if (length(parts) < 2) return(s)
    paste(parts[1], parts[length(parts)])
  }, character(1))
  unname(out)
}

attach_observer_details <- function(survey_df, observer_lookup, obs_col, prefix) {
  stopifnot(obs_col %in% names(survey_df))
  tmp <- survey_df %>%
    mutate(.obs_norm = normalize_person_name(.data[[obs_col]])) %>%
    left_join(observer_lookup, by = c(".obs_norm" = "fullName")) %>%
    select(-.obs_norm)
  lookup_cols <- setdiff(names(observer_lookup), "fullName")
  rename_map <- setNames(lookup_cols, paste0(prefix, lookup_cols))
  tmp %>% rename(!!!rename_map)
}

relocate_if_present <- function(df, cols) {
  cols <- cols[cols %in% names(df)]
  dplyr::relocate(df, dplyr::all_of(cols))
}

fish_obs_key <- fish_obs %>%
  select(fishObservationID, surveyID, species, lifeStage)

measured_counts <- fish_ind %>%
  left_join(fish_obs_key, by = "fishObservationID") %>%
  filter(!is.na(surveyID), !is.na(species)) %>%
  count(surveyID, species, lifeStage, name = "n_measured")

stopifnot("fishAddCount" %in% names(fish_add))
add_counts <- fish_add %>%
  left_join(fish_obs_key, by = "fishObservationID") %>%
  filter(!is.na(surveyID), !is.na(species)) %>%
  group_by(surveyID, species, lifeStage) %>%
  summarise(n_additional = sum(fishAddCount, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

abundance <- full_join(measured_counts, add_counts, by = c("surveyID", "species", "lifeStage")) %>%
  mutate(
    n_measured   = coalesce(n_measured, 0L),
    n_additional = coalesce(n_additional, 0),
    abundance    = n_measured + n_additional
  ) %>%
  select(surveyID, species, lifeStage, abundance, n_measured, n_additional)

survey_site <- survey %>% left_join(site, by = "siteID")

sample_event_summ <- samp_evt %>%
  group_by(surveyID) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sample_events  = n(),
    sampleEventCodes = if ("sampleEventCode" %in% names(samp_evt))
      str_c(sort(unique(na.omit(sampleEventCode))), collapse = "; ") else NA_character_,
    sampleGears = if ("sampleGear" %in% names(samp_evt))
      str_c(sort(unique(na.omit(sampleGear))), collapse = "; ") else NA_character_,
    trapCount_sum   = if ("trapCount" %in% names(samp_evt) && !all(is.na(trapCount))) sum(trapCount, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

observer_lookup <- observer %>%
  mutate(fullName = str_squish(paste(firstName, lastName))) %>%
  arrange(fullName, observerID) %>%
  group_by(fullName) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(fullName, observerID, initials, firstName, lastName, title)

survey_enriched <- survey_site
for (k in 1:4) {
  col <- paste0("observer", k)
  if (col %in% names(survey_enriched))
    survey_enriched <- attach_observer_details(survey_enriched, observer_lookup, col, paste0(col, "_"))
}

fish_survey_abundance <- abundance %>%
  left_join(survey_enriched,   by = "surveyID") %>%
  left_join(sample_event_summ, by = "surveyID") %>%
  remove_empty("cols") %>%
  relocate_if_present(c(
    "surveyID","siteID","species","lifeStage","abundance","n_measured","n_additional",
    "region","decDegLat2","decDegLon2","surveyDate","sampleGears"
  )) %>%
  filter(region == "South Central") %>%
  mutate(source = "AFFI")

fish_sc_clipped <- fish_survey_abundance %>%
  filter(!is.na(decDegLon2), !is.na(decDegLat2)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("decDegLon2", "decDegLat2"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) %>%
  st_filter(kpb_boundary)

affi_harmonized <- fish_sc_clipped |>
  mutate(siteID = as.character(siteID)) |>
  select(all_of(base_cols)) |>
  left_join(species_lookup_affi, by = "species") |>
  filter(!is.na(commonName)) |>
  select(all_of(schema_cols))

st_write(affi_harmonized, "data/input/fish_obs/affi/affi_clipped.gpkg", delete_dsn = TRUE)

title: 3  Existing Fish Observations within the Kenai Borough
text:
3.1.1 AFFI Data Interpretation
After harmonizing and clipping to the Kenai Peninsula Borough boundary, the AFFI source contributes 8,259 fish observation records to the combined dataset.
From this data subset and from discussions with ADFG staff, it does not appear that we will have existing “end of fish” or “end of anadromy” survey data to work with from AFFI. Existing data in the region is of either an opportunistic nature, or is targeted for some project-specific purpose (e.g. permitting/licensing).

3.7 Download

3.7.1 Download all fish observations
The harmonized dataset is available as a GeoPackage containing all 15006 fish observation records across all sources, clipped to the Kenai Peninsula Borough boundary.
Download kenai_fish_obs.gpkg


3.7.2 Download all anadromous fish observations


Show code
# Anadromous species as defined by ADF&G AWC species codes:
# https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/sf/SARR/AWC/index.cfm?ADFG=defs.codes
# Filter by scientificName where a binomial is available; fall back to
# commonName for the four unresolved groups (NA scientificName in lookup).
# Note: Oncorhynchus mykiss appears as "steelhead" (AWC source) and
# "rainbow trout" (KBNERR/UAF/KWF/AFFI) — both are captured via scientificName.
anadromous_sci <- c(
  "Salvelinus alpinus",        # Arctic char
  "Lethenteron camtschaticum", # Arctic lamprey
  "Coregonus autumnalis",      # Arctic cisco
  "Coregonus nasus",           # broad whitefish
  "Coregonus laurettae",       # Bering cisco
  "Oncorhynchus keta",         # chum salmon
  "Oncorhynchus kisutch",      # coho salmon
  "Oncorhynchus clarkii",      # cutthroat trout
  "Salvelinus malma",          # Dolly Varden
  "Acipenser medirostris",     # green sturgeon
  "Coregonus pidschian",       # humpback whitefish
  "Oncorhynchus tshawytscha",  # Chinook salmon
  "Coregonus sardinella",      # least cisco
  "Lethenteron ayresii",       # river lamprey
  "Spirinchus thaleichthys",   # longfin smelt
  "Osmerus mordax",            # rainbow smelt
  "Thaleichthys pacificus",    # eulachon
  "Oncorhynchus gorbuscha",    # pink salmon
  "Entosphenus tridentatus",   # Pacific lamprey
  "Oncorhynchus nerka",        # sockeye salmon
  "Stenodus leucichthys",      # inconnu
  "Oncorhynchus mykiss",       # steelhead / rainbow trout
  "Acipenser transmontanus"    # white sturgeon
)

# Unresolved groups (scientificName = NA in lookup): matched by commonName
anadromous_common_nr <- c("lamprey sp.", "smelt sp.", "sturgeon sp.", "whitefish sp.")

anadromous_clipped <- all_fish_clipped |>
  filter(scientificName %in% anadromous_sci | commonName %in% anadromous_common_nr)

unlink("data/output/kenai_anadromous_fish_obs.gpkg")
st_write(anadromous_clipped, "data/output/kenai_anadromous_fish_obs.gpkg")


Anadromous species are defined here as those listed in the ADF&G Anadromous Waters Catalog (AWC) species codes. The filtered dataset contains 13178 records across all sources. Note that Oncorhynchus mykiss appears as both “steelhead” (AWC source) and “rainbow trout” (all other sources) in this dataset; both are included since the AWC recognizes this species as anadromous, though individual survey records cannot distinguish anadromous-run fish from resident fish.

This chapter addresses the known statuses of fish presence / absence for channel segments within the project areas.
Plan:

Use results from chapter in this document, “Existing Fish Observations within the Kenai Borough”

title: 5  Field Site Selection
text:
5.1 Overview
Field crews conducting Last Fish Observed (LFO) surveys begin at a stream access point, walk upstream, and record the furthest point where fish are found. Selecting those access points is the purpose of this chapter. Sites are drawn from reaches where fish presence has not been documented, and the resulting survey data calibrate models of how far upstream anadromous fish reach in each watershed.
Two GIS files prepared in ArcGIS Pro serve as inputs: the draft NetMap stream network and a layer of AWC fish observation points snapped to the NetMap lines. From these, the script classifies reaches by fish presence status, filters to accessible candidates, extracts launch points, assigns landscape strata, and draws a proportional random sample.
Each step includes a description of the equivalent ArcGIS Pro workflow for reference.

title: 5  Field Site Selection
text:
5.1.1 Design rationale
Simple random sampling of stream reaches skews site selection toward low-elevation, high-density valley networks, which are already well-sampled. In a stratified proportional random sampling design, candidate reaches are divided into landscape strata by watershed unit, and sites are allocated in proportion to each stratum’s share of the total pool. The final sample covers the full elevational and geographic range of the study area without overrepresenting any single watershed type.


5.1.2 Workflow

title: 5  Field Site Selection
text:
5.2 Configuration
All user-adjustable parameters are set in this block. The rest of the script reads directly from these values, so changing the sample size, gradient threshold, or stratification variable requires edits only here.

title: 5  Field Site Selection
text:
5.3 Data

5.3.1 Input files
Three spatial inputs are required:



Dataset
Path
Description




Draft NetMap stream network
data/input/netmap/netmap_draft.gpkg
NetMap channel reaches for project focus HUCs


Snapped AWC fish observations
data/input/netmap/awc_snapped.gpkg
AWC fish presence points snapped to NetMap lines in ArcGIS Pro


Focus HUC boundaries
data/input/focus_hucs/focus_hucs.gpkg
Watershed polygons used for landscape stratification (Chapter 2)



The NetMap layer must include at minimum:

GRADIENT: numeric channel gradient (unitless proportion; e.g., 0.05 = 5%)
OUT_DIST: distance to river mouth in km, used to determine upstream/downstream position


# Draft NetMap stream network
streams  <- st_read("data/input/netmap/netmap_draft.gpkg")

# AWC fish observation points, pre-snapped to stream lines in ArcGIS Pro
fish_pts <- st_read("data/input/netmap/awc_snapped.gpkg")

# HUC boundaries for landscape stratification
hucs     <- st_read("data/input/focus_hucs/focus_hucs.gpkg")

# Align CRS — all subsequent operations use the streams CRS as the reference
if (st_crs(fish_pts) != st_crs(streams)) {
  fish_pts <- st_transform(fish_pts, st_crs(streams))
}
if (st_crs(hucs) != st_crs(streams)) {
  hucs <- st_transform(hucs, st_crs(streams))
}

title: 5  Field Site Selection
text:
5.5 Filter to Accessible Unknown Reaches
Two filters reduce the classified network to accessible candidates:

Fish status: keep only reaches labeled "Unknown".
Gradient: remove reaches at or above GRADIENT_MAX (default 20%), treating steep cascade segments as passage barriers.


5.5.0.1 ArcGIS Pro equivalent

Open Select By Attribute (Map tab → Selection group).
Build the expression: fishstatus = 'Unknown' AND GRADIENT < 0.20.
Use Export Features (right-click layer → Data → Export Features) to save this subset as a new layer, or continue with the selection active.







NoteGradient barriers and upstream topology



Filtering by GRADIENT < GRADIENT_MAX removes individual steep segments but does not remove flat reaches that lie upstream of a steep barrier. If a 25% gradient cascade separates a flat headwater reach from the rest of the accessible network, the attribute filter retains that headwater reach even though anadromous fish cannot reach it.
The topologically correct approach is to identify all barrier segments (GRADIENT >= GRADIENT_MAX), trace the network upstream from each barrier, and remove the entire inaccessible drainage. In ArcGIS Pro this is done with Select By Attribute → Upstream Trace → Delete. If that level of precision is needed, run that step in ArcGIS before exporting data/input/netmap/netmap_draft.gpkg. For the current implementation, the simple attribute filter is used as a practical approximation.



streams_unknown <- streams_classified |>
  filter(fishstatus == "Unknown", GRADIENT < GRADIENT_MAX)

title: 5  Field Site Selection
text:
5.6 Extract Launch Points
Each candidate reach is represented by a single launch point at its downstream end, where crews begin walking upstream. The NetMap network is digitized from mouth to source, so the start vertex of each feature (parameterization position 0) is the downstream end, consistent with OUT_DIST values being lower at the start of each line.

5.6.0.1 ArcGIS Pro equivalent

With the accessible unknown reaches selected (or as a standalone layer), open the Feature Vertices To Points tool (Data Management Tools → Features).
Input Features: the filtered stream layer. Point Type: START.
Each reach produces one point at its downstream vertex. The output inherits all attributes from the parent line.







NoteVerifying digitization direction



Before running this step, confirm that OUT_DIST values are lower at the start vertex than at the end vertex for a sample of reaches. If NetMap data for a different region are digitized in the opposite direction (source to mouth), use sample = 1 instead of sample = 0 to extract the correct downstream end.



launch_points <- streams_unknown |>
  mutate(geometry = st_line_sample(geometry, sample = 0)) |>
  # Drop any reaches for which a vertex could not be extracted
  filter(!st_is_empty(geometry))

title: 5  Field Site Selection
text:
5.7 Landscape Stratification
Each launch point is assigned to the watershed unit (HUC) it falls within. The HUC name is the stratification variable used in the quota calculation below. Points outside all HUC polygons are dropped; these are typically edge-of-study-area reaches whose downstream vertex falls just outside the boundary.

5.7.0.1 ArcGIS Pro equivalent

Open the Spatial Join tool (Analysis Tools → Overlay).
Target Features: the launch points layer. Join Features: the HUC boundary polygons.
Join Operation: One to One. Match Option: Within (or Intersect if some points fall on polygon boundaries).
The output contains all HUC polygon attributes (including the stratification field, e.g., huc_name) joined to each launch point.
Use Select By Attribute to remove any records where the stratification field is null (points that fell outside all polygons).


points_stratified <- st_join(launch_points, hucs, join = st_within) |>
  filter(!is.na(.data[[STRATIFY_BY]]))

title: 5  Field Site Selection
5  Field Site Selection
text:
5.9 Output
The final point layer is exported as a GeoPackage.

5.9.0.1 ArcGIS Pro equivalent
Right-click the final point layer in the Contents pane → Data → Export Features. Set the output location to data/output/field_sites/ and the format to GeoPackage.

st_write(
  field_sites,
  "data/output/field_sites/stratified_survey_sites.gpkg",
  delete_layer = TRUE
)



5.9.1 Site allocation summary

strata_summary |>
  select(
    Stratum             = all_of(STRATIFY_BY),
    `Available reaches` = n,
    Proportion          = prop,
    `Sites allocated`   = quota
  ) |>
  mutate(Proportion = scales::percent(Proportion, accuracy = 0.1)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Stratified site allocation by watershed unit.",
    align   = c("l", "r", "r", "r")
  )



5.9.2 Map

library(leaflet)
library(RColorBrewer)

# Reproject to WGS84 for leaflet
field_sites_wgs <- st_transform(field_sites, 4326)
hucs_wgs        <- st_transform(hucs, 4326)

# Color palette keyed to strata
strata_levels <- unique(field_sites_wgs[[STRATIFY_BY]])
pal <- colorFactor(
  palette = brewer.pal(min(length(strata_levels), 8), "Dark2"),
  domain  = strata_levels
)

leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldTopoMap") |>
  addPolygons(
    data        = hucs_wgs,
    weight      = 1.5,
    color       = "#555",
    fillOpacity = 0.05,
    label       = ~hucs_wgs[[STRATIFY_BY]]
  ) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    data        = field_sites_wgs,
    radius      = 5,
    color       = ~pal(.data[[STRATIFY_BY]]),
    stroke      = FALSE,
    fillOpacity = 0.85,
    label       = ~paste0(.data[[STRATIFY_BY]], " | OUT_DIST: ",
                          round(OUT_DIST, 1), " km")
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    pal    = pal,
    values = field_sites_wgs[[STRATIFY_BY]],
    title  = "Watershed stratum"
  )

title: 5  Field Site Selection
text:
5.4 Network Classification
Reaches are labeled "Present" if they fall at or downstream of a documented fish observation, or "Unknown" if they lie above all documented observations. Only "Unknown" reaches are sampled in subsequent steps.
Because the fish points have been snapped to the NetMap lines, each point sits on exactly one reach. Any reach with an OUT_DIST value greater than the highest OUT_DIST among fish-bearing reaches is labeled "Unknown": it lies further from the river mouth and therefore above all confirmed fish observations.

5.4.0.1 ArcGIS Pro equivalent

Open Select By Location (Map tab → Selection group).
Input Features: stream network layer. Relationship: Intersect. Selecting Features: AWC fish observation points.
Open the Attribute Table for the stream layer. With the fish-bearing reaches selected, open Calculate Field, set the field to fishstatus, and enter the expression "Present".
Click Switch Selection at the top of the attribute table to invert the selection.
Run Calculate Field again on fishstatus with the expression "Unknown".
Click Clear Selection.







NoteClassification and branching networks



The OUT_DIST approach correctly identifies the most-upstream fish observation across the entire network, but labels all reaches above that threshold as "Unknown" regardless of which tributary they are on. In a branching network, reaches on tributaries that have never been surveyed are labeled "Unknown", which is the right call for field planning. Reaches on a different branch than the most-upstream observation may be labeled "Present" when they are arguably untested; the ArcGIS Pro Trace Network approach described in Chapter 4 handles this more rigorously.



# Find which reaches contain at least one snapped fish observation
fish_reach_ids <- st_intersects(streams, fish_pts) |>
  lengths() > 0

# The OUT_DIST of the most-upstream fish-bearing reach sets the classification threshold
fish_outdist_threshold <- streams |>
  filter(fish_reach_ids) |>
  pull(OUT_DIST) |>
  max(na.rm = TRUE)

# Classify all reaches relative to that threshold
streams_classified <- streams |>
  mutate(
    fishstatus = if_else(OUT_DIST > fish_outdist_threshold, "Unknown", "Present")
  )
